title: Reverse Linked List
statement: You are given a linked list as a Python list of values. Implement `reverse_list(values)` that conceptually reverses the list order and returns the reversed values. Internally think in terms of prev/curr/next pointers.

predict_steps.prompt: Before rewiring curr.next, what must you save?
After pointing curr.next to prev, what becomes the new curr?

learn_quiz.question: Why save `nxt = curr.next` first?
choices: So you do not lose the rest of the list

learn_quiz.question: At the end, which pointer is the new head?

viva.question: What is the time and space cost of iteratively reversing a linked list?
What are the head and next of an empty list or a one-node list after reverse?
Why must you save curr.next before rewiring curr.next to prev?
expected_points: otherwise lose the rest of the list
